data.narrative:
Anduril Industries, a Series H defense and security company founded by Palmer Luckey, Brian Schimpf, Trae Stephens, Matt Grimm, and Joe Chen, is currently valued at $61B following $11B+ in total capital raised. The target operates within a Defense & Security sector comprising 22 same-sector peers, though the comparable universe for narrowly-filtered valuation work remains constrained.

A peer-median triangulation approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient datapoint density. The analysis identified only 2 public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers, with none satisfying simultaneous filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier criteria—falling below the minimum three-datapoint threshold for reliable statistical inference. The broader peer set includes Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, Quantum-Systems, and Flock Safety, but heterogeneity in financing stage, revenue scale, and technology focus limits direct comparability.

The absence of sufficient narrowly-filtered peers represents the primary valuation constraint. At $61B, Anduril occupies an outlier position within frontier defense-tech, making traditional comparable-company analysis unreliable. Any valuation work would require either (1) application of revenue-multiple or margin-based methods if operating metrics become available, or (2) explicit scenario modeling around defense procurement and TAM expansion. The current valuation's defensibility hinges on forward-looking contract pipelines and market share expectations rather than peer-benchmarked metrics.
